newsitem.title: USA: Profit Recovery unsure about Q3 views.
newsitem.headline: Profit Recovery unsure about Q3 views.

text.p: Profit Recovery Group International Inc said Wednesday it is not sure whether it will meet analysts' expectations for its third quarter.

Separately, the company also announced that a recent sharp decline in the price of its stock was most likely due to the company's absence from an investment conference, as well as an error in the reporting of a block trade.
The company said it was "hopeful of achieving" the consensus analysts' earnings-per-share estimate, but that the results would depend on its revenues in the rest of September.
First Call analysts' estimates project per-share earnings of $0.15 in the third quarter. Year-ago comparisons were not appropriate as the company first offered shares to the public in March.
"The company is currently unable to determine whether or not the analysts' expectations will be met," Profit Recovery Group said in a statement accompanying the announcement.

The company said revenues were below plan for the first half of the 1996 third quarter but that they are above plan in the second half of the quarter, adding "management is hopeful that these increases will continue through the end of the quarter."
The period's revenues were hurt by delays in three large domestic audit engagements. Two of those jobs had begun and the third was expected to begin soon, the company said.

The company said it also experienced an unexpected reduction in the number of days worked by domestic auditors during the month of July, as well as higher-than-expected expenses in the quarter, including "significant unbudgeted investments in information technology."

In reference to its share price, Profit Recovery said its decision not to attend the investment conference Tuesday was "based upon scheduling difficulties of the company's management and the company's inability to comment definitively on its third quarter performance."
The company also said it was informed that a block trade on September 23 was incorrectly reported as one million shares instead of 100,000 shares.
"The company is unaware of any senior officers or board members...who have sold PRGX shares during the current quarter-to-date," Profit Recovery added.
